title: GATE CS Preparation: A Subject-by-Subject Study Order
description: A GATE CS preparation order built from the official 2027 syllabus: which of the ten sections to study first, which ones depend on each other, and a 17-week plan to the exam.
author: Studyloaf Team

content.body: The GATE CS 2027 syllabus has ten sections, and several of them lean on each other. Studying them in an order that respects those links saves you from learning the same idea twice. This order is built from the official 2027 CS syllabus text, not from any guess about which sections carry more marks: GATE doesn't publish that split.

content.heading: The marks you can count on
content.body: GATE CS is 100 marks: General Aptitude 15, Engineering Mathematics 13, and 72 for the other nine sections. General Aptitude and Engineering Mathematics together are 28 marks, so they deserve steady time from the first week, not a cram at the end.

table.caption: A dependency-based order for the GATE CS 2027 sections
rows: Discrete Mathematics (from Engineering Mathematics); Programming and Data Structures
Recurrence relations and graphs feed Algorithms, and logic and sets feed Theory of Computation. Data structures are what algorithms run on
Algorithms; Digital Logic
Algorithms builds on data structures and recurrences. Digital Logic stands alone and is needed for the next phase
Computer Organization and Architecture; Theory of Computation
ALU and control unit design build on combinational and sequential circuits. TOC builds on logic and sets
Operating System; Compiler Design
Virtual memory and I/O scheduling build on the memory hierarchy, interrupts and DMA. Lexical analysis and parsing build on finite automata and context-free grammars
Databases; Computer Networks
Indexing with B and B+ trees uses trees from data structures, and concurrency control echoes OS synchronization. Networks is the most self-contained section
Linear Algebra, Calculus, Probability and Statistics
The rest of Engineering Mathematics, which no later section depends on, so it can sit late or run alongside

content.heading: Worked example: a 17-week plan
content.body: From 7 October 2026 there are 17 weeks and 3 days to Saturday 6 February 2027. One way to spend them: phases 1 to 6 take two weeks each, except phase 1 which takes three, so the syllabus is covered by the end of week 13. Weeks 14 to 17 are for revision and full-length 3-hour papers. General Aptitude gets two short sessions every week throughout, because its four sections (verbal, quantitative, analytical and spatial) reward regular practice more than a late cram.

table.caption: The 17-week GATE CS plan
rows: 1 to 3
Discrete Mathematics; Programming and Data Structures
4 to 5
Algorithms; Digital Logic
6 to 7
Computer Organization and Architecture; Theory of Computation
8 to 9
Operating System; Compiler Design
Databases; Computer Networks
Linear Algebra, Calculus, Probability and Statistics; catch-up
Revision, previous papers and full-length timed papers

content.heading: Stay on the 2027 syllabus
list: Computer Networks lists IPv4 (fragmentation, CIDR notation, network address translation) and TCP flow and congestion control, plus DNS and HTTP. IPv6 isn't listed
Programming and Data Structures lists trees, binary search trees and binary heaps. B and B+ trees appear under Databases, as indexing
Compiler Design includes runtime environments, intermediate code generation and data flow analyses such as liveness analysis
Operating System includes system calls, inter-process communication and CPU and I/O scheduling

content.heading: Common mistakes
list: Starting with Compiler Design or Operating System before the sections they build on
Leaving all of Engineering Mathematics to the end. Discrete Mathematics is needed early
Studying topics from an old syllabus that the 2027 PDF doesn't list
Skipping full-length practice. Every paper is 3 hours, and stamina is part of the test
